simple.meaning: לָהַהּ (lâhahh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be rabid (figuratively, insane); also (from the exhaustion of frenzy) to languish.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Genesis, Proverbs, beginning at Genesis 47:13. Its contexts include family line, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָהַהּ (H3856).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: לָהַהּ (lâhahh) / H3856 is traced through Genesis 47:13, Proverbs 26:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to be rabid (figuratively, insane); also (from the exhaustion of frenzy) to languish
definitions.full: H3856. lahah [ לָהָה ] verb languish, faint (= לָאָה ) ( לְהִי ᵑ7 , id. ; — Qal Imperfect 3feminine singular with apocope אֶרֶץ וַתֵּ֫לַהּ Gen 47:13 (of famine). [ לִהְלֵהַּ ] verb quadriliteral amaze, startle (compare Syriac Palpel confudit, obstupefecit ; Ethpalpel stupore percussus est ; consternatio , all in Lexicons, PS 1894 ) — Hithpalpel Participle מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ as substantive = madman , followed by זִקִים הַיֹּרֶה Prov Gen 26:18 (see Now).
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root meaning properly, to burn , i.e. (by implication)

occurrences.englishText: There was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
